title: Jank during canvas moves
question: Long frames per second, moving against still (jank), and the party of the scripts in the moving frames (frames, scripts).

issues.text: One session is a handful of minutes and a few moves; long frames cluster at load.
issues.fix: Leave out the first 10 s (load) and compare rates over several sessions.

issues.text: A long frame during a move may be caused by work the move didn't start (a timer, a query answer).
issues.fix: Read the frame's span and script: a pan's own work is the canvas transform and the graphs it redraws.

alternatives.question: Which graph's draws (spans) cost the most frames?
Is the same dashboard smooth on another machine or browser?
alternatives.why: Expands to the hardware and browser the numbers depend on.

hypotheses.statement: Long frames come more often per second while the canvas moves than while it stands still.
hypotheses.null: The rate of long frames is the same moving and still.

concepts.label: Long animation frame
concepts.description: A frame of 50 ms or more.

concepts.label: Canvas interaction
concepts.description: Moving or still, from the canvas's pans, zooms and drags.

concepts.label: Script attribution
concepts.description: The party of a frame's scripts.

method.summary: Long frames per second of moving time against per second of still time (Poisson rates).

steps.title: Moving or still
steps.detail: moving per entry, from the canvas move intervals (jank).

steps.title: Rates
steps.detail: long_frames over moving_s and over the still seconds (session length minus moving_s).

steps.title: Who to fix
steps.detail: If moving frames are long, read their span and scripts (frames, scripts).

caveats: Chrome/Edge only for LoAF scripts and Event Timing.
The machine, other tabs and extensions change every number.
The profiler's own redraws are in the data.
